extra.message: Server-Side Template Injection. The `name` query parameter (declared at line 19) is interpolated with an f-string into `content` at line 38, and that attacker-controlled string is then compiled and executed as a Jinja2 template via `Template(content).render()`. A request such as `/?name={{7*6}}` is evaluated by the template engine; Jinja2 sandbox escapes (e.g. `{{ ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__() }}` or `{{ cycler.__init__.__globals__.os.popen('id').read() }}`) allow arbitrary code execution in the application process. The upstream Coraza WAF rule intended to block this (caddy/Caddyfile:17) is inert because `SecRuleEngine Off` is set.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine
CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: Reflected cross-site scripting. The user-supplied `name` query parameter is concatenated into an HTML document with an f-string without any HTML escaping, and the result is returned with `response_class=HTMLResponse` (line 18) so the browser renders it as HTML. Because the value is injected into the template *source* and rendered with a bare `jinja2.Template` (no autoescape and no escaping of the already-inlined value), a request like `/?name=<script>alert(document.cookie)</script>` executes attacker script in the victim's browser origin.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: Hardcoded secret token. `SUPER_SECRET_TOKEN = "5u93R53Cr3tT0k3n"` embeds a credential directly in source code that is committed to version control (the `FIXME` comment shows the intended `os.getenv("SUPER_SECRET_TOKEN")` lookup was disabled). Anyone with read access to the repository, the built container image, or the Python bytecode obtains the token, and it cannot be rotated without a code change and redeploy. `SUPER_SECRET_NAME` on line 13 is hardcoded the same way.

Active debug functionality reachable in production. The FastAPI/Starlette application is constructed with `debug=config.DEBUG`, and `config.DEBUG` (app/config.py:9) is taken straight from the `DEBUG` environment variable with no environment/production guard; `docker-compose.yaml:4` passes `DEBUG` through to the running container. When enabled, Starlette replaces the generic 500 handler with an interactive debug page that renders full stack traces, source-code context and local variable values of the failing frame to any remote client, disclosing internal paths and in-scope secrets (e.g. `config.SUPER_SECRET_TOKEN`).

cwe: CWE-215: Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Debugging Code

extra.message: The Coraza WAF is loaded with `SecRuleEngine Off`, which disables rule enforcement entirely. Every protective rule defined immediately below it (id:1001 SSTI, id:1002 SQL injection, id:1003 XSS, id:1004 path traversal, at lines 17-20) is therefore never evaluated or enforced, even though each is written with `deny,status:403`. This misconfiguration silently removes the only compensating control in front of the application and leaves the SSTI and XSS flaws in `app/main.py` directly exploitable through both the `localhost` and `:1337` site blocks.

cwe: CWE-1188: Initialization of a Resource with an Insecure Default

extra.message: `SecDebugLogLevel 9` sets the Coraza WAF debug log to its most verbose level in the deployed reverse-proxy configuration. Combined with `SecRequestBodyAccess On` (line 15), this writes full request URIs, arguments and request bodies of every proxied request into the proxy log, so any credentials, tokens or personal data submitted by clients are persisted in plaintext logs and exposed to anyone able to read container logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: Outbound HTTP request without a timeout. `requests.get(config.PUBLIC_IP_SERVICE_URL)` is issued on every request to `/` with no `timeout=` argument, so `requests` waits indefinitely for the remote host. Because this is a blocking call inside an `async def` route handler, it also blocks the event loop rather than just one worker. A slow, unresponsive or attacker-influenced `PUBLIC_IP_SERVICE_URL` host (a slowloris-style peer that accepts the connection and never responds) causes every concurrent request to `/` to hang and exhausts the server, a denial of service reachable by any unauthenticated client.
